paper_summary: Al 7075 matrix syntactic foams filled with recycled expanded-glass (EG) spheres of 0.5-1, 1-2 and 2-4 mm were produced for the first time on a fully automated industrial cold-chamber high-pressure die casting machine, and the casting parameters (casting temperature, injection pressure, piston speed, filler preheat temperature, piston waiting time) were optimised for each filler size. Nine flawless 60 x 80 mm cylinders were cast with densities of 1.82-2.06 g/cm3 (mean 1.93), EG volume fractions of 34.5-45.6 % and total porosities of 27.2-35.9 %. Smaller EG spheres gave lower density and higher porosity but needed higher injection pressure, piston speed, preheat and waiting time; injection pressure and piston speed were the most influential parameters on density, which rose to as much as 2.14 g/cm3 when they were raised. The study is fabrication/characterisation only - no mechanical tests were run.

processing.particle_grade: recycled expanded glass (EG) spheres, Omnis Composite Ltd; 73 wt% SiO2, 14 wt% Na2O, 8 wt% CaO, 4 wt% MgO, 0.15 wt% Al2O3, 0.1 wt% Fe2O3; size range 0.5-1 mm

structure.microstructure_notes: Total porosity 33.8 % (= 0.338 as a fraction), calculated from Eq. (3) as the EG volume fraction times (1 - rho_fil/rho_solid); this is the intended porosity contributed by the porous EG spheres, not unintended matrix voiding, so it is reported here rather than in matrix_porosity_fraction. EG spheres have a thin-walled outer surface and a porous inner structure; supplier bulk density 0.2-0.35 g/cm3 and thermal conductivity 0.065 W/mK (particle property, not the foam). Optical/SEM images show metallic matrix plus porous EG spheres with secondary phases: combined/agglomerated particles, broken sphere fragments and matrix-filled spheres; small shrinkage cavities can form at the matrix/filler interface and molten Al can partially penetrate EG pores, raising density.

test.specimen_notes: Cylindrical casting 60 mm diameter x 80 mm length, cold-chamber high-pressure die casting (die and sprue preheated to ~300 C, solidification ~30 s). Optimised parameters for this filler size: injection pressure 210 bar, piston speed 40 mm/s, EG preheat 600 C, piston waiting time 30 s, casting temperature 730 C. Characterisation only: density by mass/cylindrical volume, EG volume fraction and total porosity from Eqs. (1)-(3), plus optical and SEM microscopy. No mechanical testing was performed in this paper, hence test_type='other'.

extraction_notes: This is a processing/characterisation paper: it reports NO mechanical or thermal property of the foams, so every Properties field is null in all records. All ten records therefore carry test_type='other' with specimen_notes explaining that only density, volume fraction, porosity and microscopy were measured. Records 1-9 are the nine foams of Table 2 (verbatim density, EG volume fraction converted from % to fraction, total porosity). Record 10 is the 2.14 g/cm3 maximum density stated in the Conclusions for the extra 2-4 mm samples of the Fig. 8 injection-parameter series; its process point is only shown graphically, so confidence is low and volume fraction/porosity are null. particle_type='other' rather than 'ceramic_hollow' or 'glass_microballoon': the expanded-glass granules are millimetre-scale porous (foamed) glass spheres with a thin dense outer skin, not hollow-shell microballoons; 'ceramic_hollow' would be the nearest enum if a hollow-particle class must be assigned. particle_mean_diameter_um is the arithmetic midpoint of the paper's stated size band (0.5-1 mm -> 750 um, 1-2 mm -> 1500 um, 2-4 mm -> 3000 um); the paper reports only ranges, never a mean, so treat these as derived. particle_true_density_g_cc left null: the paper quotes 0.2-0.35 g/cm3 as the supplier BULK (poured) density of the EG granules, which is not the particle true density. Total porosity is placed in microstructure_notes, not matrix_porosity_fraction, because it is the intended porosity of the EG filler (Eq. 3) rather than unintended matrix voiding. process_route='pressure_infiltration' is the closest enum value; the actual route is industrial cold-chamber high-pressure die casting, in which a piston pressure-infiltrates molten Al into a preheated bed of EG spheres (die/sprue preheated ~300 C). cure_or_process_temperature_c is the casting temperature: 730 C for the 0.5-1 and 1-2 mm foams and 720 C for the 2-4 mm foams, per Sec. 3.3. NOTE an internal inconsistency - Sec. 3.1 states 'all the casting processes, regardless of filler size, were carried out at 730 C', which contradicts the 720 C given in Sec. 3.3 for the 2-4 mm foams; Sec. 3.3 was followed as it is the size-specific statement. A second internal inconsistency: Sec. 3.2 says foam density AND total porosity both rise with EG sphere size, but Table 2 (and the Conclusions) show porosity FALLS as sphere size rises; Table 2 numbers were taken as authoritative. A third: the Conclusions call 45.6 % the 'highest porosity value' of SF3, but 45.6 % is SF3's EG volume fraction - its total porosity is 35.9 %; Table 2 was followed. Table 1 (process trials P1-P10 for the 1-2 mm filler) was transcribed but generates no records because no density or property value is reported per trial - only a pass/fail visual assessment in Fig. 3. The P10 combination (730 C, 200 bar, 30 mm/s, 550 C preheat, 20 s) is recorded in specimen_notes for the 1-2 mm foams as the stated optimum.
